task: Review the consent rules for a reorganisation of the provider in CONTRACT-01 for the customer. Does an internal reorganisation require consent? Ownership and continued responsibility are not yet confirmed.

actual_tool_result.text: Neither party may assign any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other party. In addition, Provider must obtain Customer’s prior written consent before a change of control of Provider takes effect. That consent is not required for a reorganization within a wholly owned group if Provider remains responsible for its obligations under this Agreement. Any attempted but non-permitted assignment is void. This Agreement will be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their permitted successors and assigns.

DRAFT REVIEW – CONTRACT-01 (Provider reorganisation)

Source inspected: KT-1 (Key Terms change replacing Section 12.6).

Consent triggers identified:
1. Assignment – prior written consent of Customer required for any assignment of rights or obligations.
2. Change of control – Customer's prior written consent required before a change of control of Provider takes effect.

Exception (KT-1): Consent is not required for a reorganisation within a wholly owned group if Provider remains responsible for its obligations under this Agreement.

Application to the proposed internal reorganisation:
• The label 'internal reorganisation' does not, by itself, establish whether the transaction constitutes an assignment or a change of control.
• Whether the group exception applies cannot be confirmed: (a) wholly owned group membership is not established, and (b) continued responsibility of Provider is not yet confirmed.

Conclusion: The consent position cannot be determined on available facts.

Evidence requested: Please provide transaction details showing (i) whether the reorganisation involves an assignment of contractual rights/obligations or a change in control of Provider, (ii) whether Provider and the relevant entities are within a wholly owned group, and (iii) whether Provider will remain responsible for its obligations post-transaction.
